text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained modestly today (up 0.4%), continuing a sharp recovery from last week's dip. The stock has climbed about $42 in five trading days, rebounding from November 6's low of $372.74. This bounce reflects tightening refining margins: U.S. crude is trading at $89.62 per barrel while heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year, signaling strong demand for refined products heading into winter. Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, leaving little room to increase output and supporting margins for those already operating at full throttle.

The broader backdrop of rising heating oil prices and near-peak refinery utilization should favor Marathon's profitability over the coming weeks. However, the recent news that Russian crude production has rebounded and global oil markets are shifting back toward surplus could eventually pressure margins if supply growth outpaces demand — something worth watching in coming weeks.
